articleTitle: Water trees-can they be predicted or detected?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: The deterioration of polymeric insulation by the growth of water trees has been investigated for the last 20 years. It is known that water tree growth occurs in service, reduces the breakdown strength of the insulation and can reduce the service life. The author investigates test methods to see if water trees can be predicted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric performance of gas-insulated switchgear and possible methods of on-line monitoring
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: The dielectric performance of gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) is critical to its long term service integrity. Many parameters that are of little significance to open type air insulated switchgear are of vital importance to GIS. Detailed on-site examination is necessary to ensure chamber cleanliness during site erection as a foreign object left inside can in itself induce dielectric breakdown. In addition loose, or ineffectively bonded, line or earth side components can vibrate under the effects of both magnetic and electrostatic forces to induce partial discharge activity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing to breakdown-what does this tell us?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: Tests to establish a breakdown strength generally fall into one of three categories: establishment of suitability for an application; performance and quality tests for a given design; and proof tests to verify the quality of an item before it is released to the customer. The probability of failure in constant stress tests using the Weibull distribution is also looked at.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: Thermosetting and thermoplastic organic insulating polymers are both subject to either tracking or erosion processes when a surface discharge occurs on them. Pre-discharge and post-discharge characteristics are described for both tracking and erosion processes. Three test methods for assessing the performance of organic materials under polluted conditions are presented. They are: a comparative tracking index test; an inclined-plane test; and a dust-fog test.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Diagnosis of PD in oil impregnated insulation using digital measurement techniques
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: The development of digital techniques offers the possibility of recording all the data concerning partial discharges during a test. The author considers a diagnosis method applied to the insulation of the power transformer alone. After using the measuring system on several paper and oil transformers, it is obvious that a software tool will permit the differentiation of discharge sources.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The influence of polymer contamination on breakdown characteristics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: Whilst the range of possible contaminants in polymers is extensive, certain types have been observed to occur more frequently. The authors characterise the relative effects on dielectric strength of the more common inclusion, that of irregular shaped aluminium particles approximately 10-150 mu m in size. A bond percolation model is used to analyse failure measurements of polyethylene plaques containing a known volume fraction of aluminium particles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Assessment of machine and transformer insulation
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: Complex insulation assemblies such as transformers and rotating machines, apart from having to meet specified outputs, are required to operate virtually continuously for long periods of time. Many customers seek to operate their machines well beyond their design life through maintenance and refurbishment. An important factor in determining life is the insulation system, though this does not necessarily limit life. The author describes acceptance tests and in-service tests for the assessment of insulation quality in machines and transformers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: The electrical detection of individual partial discharges from high power electrical plant insulation has proved to be an effective method of monitoring a stress condition which can cause severe degradation and possibly failure of plant insulation. In addition, such measurements can provide a basis for assessing the overall integrity of the insulating system since degradation of the system, irrespective of the particular causative stress, almost always results in partial discharge activity. The nature of the discharge pattern can provide valuable information on the form and extent of degradation and, in some instances, on its location.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electrical testing of polymeric insulated cables for life prediction
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Insulation Diagnostics - Methods for Determining Quality, Remnant Life and Proof Testing
abstract: The design of the insulation system of medium and high voltage electric cables is mostly governed by the test conditions imposed on the cable during type tests, routine post manufacturing tests and post installation commissioning tests. Currently, there is strong technical and commercial pressure to widen the application of polymeric insulation to higher voltage (and higher stressed) cables called upon to work in more arduous conditions with less protection from their installation environments. The authors describe a situation where reliability was of paramount importance, the subject was a 70 mm/sup 2/ solid copper conductor triplex extruded cable with conducting polymer screens and insulated with an EP rubber.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
